speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition, can you describe exactly what the vertigo feels like—does the room seem to be spinning around you, or do you feel like you are spinning? Also, did this episode start suddenly while you were resting or during a specific movement?

speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with a sudden-onset sensation that the room is spinning, leading to several episodes of nausea and vomiting. The symptoms started as he was going to bed and lasted for approximately 3 minutes. He mentions that he has never experienced anything like this before and currently feels at his baseline.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any hearing loss, ringing in the ears, or a feeling of fullness in your ears on either side? Additionally, have you experienced any headaches, difficulty speaking, weakness, or numbness in your face or limbs?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Sudden-onset sensation of the room spinning. I also have Nausea, Vomiting, Dizziness.

speaker: Doctor
text: Did this episode occur after a specific change in head position, such as rolling over in bed or looking up? Also, do you currently have any hearing loss, ringing in your ears, or a feeling of fullness in one or both ears?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: The patient is otherwise healthy with only a history of eczema. No prior episodes of similar nature. Social history: No significant social history provided.

speaker: Doctor
text: Did the spinning sensation stop when you kept your head still, or did it continue regardless of your position? Also, do you have any current hearing loss, ringing in your ears, or a feeling of fullness?

speaker: Patient
text: Denies headaches, hearing loss, tinnitus, loss of consciousness or neurological deficits.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the brief duration of symptoms and the absence of neurological signs or auditory deficits, BPPV remains the primary suspect. REQUEST TEST: Dix-Hallpike_Manoeuvre

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Positive, inducing nystagmus and reproducing patient’s symptoms of vertigo when head is turned to the left and laid back.

speaker: Doctor
text: The positive Dix-Hallpike maneuver confirms Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV) affecting the left posterior semicircular canal. DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV)
